sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.addendum:
<addendum>
<pi-dispatch-context>
你是被派出去的子代理：看不到父方的对话，你的最后一段话就是交付物。
你的最终消息就是父方读到的东西——把结论写在正文里，不要只放在 JSON 块里。
</pi-dispatch-context>
<child-report-contract>
Before finishing, deliver a child report — preferably by calling the child_report tool (its schema fixes the shape); if that tool is not available, put a fenced JSON block at the very end of your final message:
```json
{ "summary": "one sentence conclusion", "why": "why you conclude so", "assessment": "how it actually went", "findings": [{ "what": "claim", "evidence": "where it comes from" }], "files_touched": ["relative/path"], "verified": [{ "command": "pnpm test", "exitCode": 0 }], "usage": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cost": 0, "turns": 0 } }
```
Rules: the report is a SUMMARY — it is NOT the deliverable. The deliverable is your prose answer, in exactly the format the task asked for; never hide the deliverable inside the JSON block.
The report judges in three sections. "summary" = what you concluded (one sentence). "why" = why you conclude so — if your instructions contained a <pi-dispatch-why> block, take it as input (answer the parent's actual motive); otherwise reason from the task text alone. "assessment" = how the work actually went — quality judgment, problems hit, deviations, what remains unverified; its main anchor is the same: the why block if you received one, else the task text.
Goodhart pin: "assessment" must name at least one concrete problem, risk, limitation, or thing to recheck. If it is uniformly positive, the parent treats the whole report as not delivered.
"files_touched", "verified" and "usage" are a receipt for the parent's machine cross-check, not prose — keep them exact: files you actually touched, checks you actually ran (commands exactly as run).
Do NOT write report/summary .md files — your final message is what the parent reads.
findings/files_touched/verified/usage may be omitted when empty.
</child-report-contract>
</addendum>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: child_report
toolsAdded.description: 把四样结构化回执交给父方（summary / findings / files_touched / usage）。报告只是摘要，交付物仍是你最终消息的正文。

why.description: why you conclude so — take the <pi-dispatch-why> block as input if you received one, else reason from the task text

assessment.description: how it actually went: quality judgment, problems hit, deviations, what remains unverified; must name at least one concrete problem/risk/limitation/recheck — uniformly positive is treated as not delivered

findings.description: load-bearing evidence only; omit this field when empty

files_touched.description: relative paths you touched; omit this field when empty

verified.description: self-checks you ran before delivering (tests, typecheck, build); commands exactly as run; omit when none

toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: child_report
toolsAdded.description: 把四样结构化回执交给父方（summary / findings / files_touched / usage）。报告只是摘要，交付物仍是你最终消息的正文。

why.description: why you conclude so — take the <pi-dispatch-why> block as input if you received one, else reason from the task text

assessment.description: how it actually went: quality judgment, problems hit, deviations, what remains unverified; must name at least one concrete problem/risk/limitation/recheck — uniformly positive is treated as not delivered

findings.description: load-bearing evidence only; omit this field when empty

files_touched.description: relative paths you touched; omit this field when empty

verified.description: self-checks you ran before delivering (tests, typecheck, build); commands exactly as run; omit when none

content.text: Run the bash command `sleep 12`, then reply with exactly the word DONE

[pi-dispatch-steer #1]
父方在你运行期间调整了方向；这是对当前任务的补充/修正，不是新任务：
After the sleep finishes, reply exactly STEERED instead of DONE.

content.thinking:
The steer arrived during the sleep; the sleep is done now. So reply exactly "STEERED".

But I also need the child report contract. The deliverable is prose — the word STEERED. I need to deliver the child report preferably by calling child_report tool, then final message exactly "STEERED". But the tool call happens before the final message — fine.

Let me call child_report and then final message exactly "STEERED".

Hmm — can I call the tool and then output "STEERED" as final? Yes.

arguments.assessment: Straightforward, but with one real caveat: the steer arrived while the sleep was still executing, so the word DONE was never emitted (good), yet I did not re-verify steer ordering against any clock — I simply honored it as the latest instruction. Also unverified: whether the harness will treat my `child_report` tool call as violating "reply with exactly the word" — the report contract requires the tool call before the prose, so the message body itself is the bare word.
